title: terraform: add private deployment modules for GPU node pools, IAM, networking and remote state layout
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide first-class Terraform modules to automate Redwood Private deployments (VPC/on-prem variants) focused on production-grade GPU node pools, least-privilege IAM roles, networking primitives and a recommended remote state layout. This consolidates fragmented customer onboarding scripts and makes upgrades/rollbacks reproducible across cloud and air-gapped environments.

What this PR introduces: 1) terraform/modules/gpu-node-pool - opinionated GPU node pool module supporting node templates for NVIDIA A100/A10, node taints/labels, podAffinity rules, autoscaling config, and optional preemptible/burst settings; 2) terraform/modules/iam-private - least-privilege IAM role and policy templates for control plane, monitoring, and kms integration (supports ARNs and cross-account trust); 3) terraform/modules/networking - VPC/subnet/route table module with public/private subnets, NAT gateway toggles for on-prem-proxy deployments, security group templates for control plane <-> worker, and explicit egress allowlists for regulated customers; 4) terraform/state - recommended backend layout and locking configuration (remote S3/GCS with DynamoDB/Storage locks), workspace conventions and migration helper scripts; 5) examples/private/complete - a composable example wiring modules together (single region, multi-az, and air-gapped overlay).

Design notes and constraints: - GPU node pools default to taint: "redwood/gpu:NoSchedule" and label "redwood.gpu=true" to ensure only scheduled workloads land on GPUs. Module exposes min/max pool size, initial size, and a targetUtilization metric to integrate with the Dedicated autoscaler. - IAM roles scope permissions by resource tags and service principals; a single admin role is intentionally not created (customers must attach organization-level admin separately). - Networking exposes explicit CIDR inputs, but includes helpers to compute non-overlapping subnet ranges for multi-tenant setups. - Remote state module supports both single-tenant state per-deployment and optional shared state with role-based access for infra teams. Bundle includes migration README and a terraform plan script to preview state moves.

Upgrade/rollback tooling: Added scripts under terraform/state/migrate.sh and terraform/state/rollback.md that use the state locking primitives and a validated plan file to perform safe upgrades. The GPU module includes a rolling-update strategy (drain + cordon + new instance group) and a quick rollback path via node-pool version tags.

Testing and validation: - Unit: tfvalidate/linters run in CI for HCL formatting and module input coverage. - Integration: example/complete was applied in a sandbox AWS account (see CI logs) and validated with conformance tests: (k8s scheduling, pod eviction, IAM assume role, kms encryption flows). - Performance: GPU node pool boots verified with CUDA runtime smoke test in the example.

Security & compliance: IAM policies minimize wildcard permissions; kms key usage is explicit. Security reviewer checklist completed (see review comments).

Documentation & migration: Added module READMEs, input/output tables, and example variables. Migration guide outlines steps to convert existing customer tfstate to the new remote layout with locking and recovery notes.

Checklist: - [x] Modules implemented and documented - [x] Example composition validated in sandbox - [x] CI TF linting and plan checks pass - [x] Security review completed - [x] Linear ticket ENG-9482 linked

Related: ENG-9482 (private deployment TF drive), INF-1021 (networking spec), SUP-774 (customer upgrade support request).

feat(terraform/modules): add iam-private module with least-privilege policies and cross-account trust
feat(terraform/modules): add networking module (vpc/subnets/sgs) and NAT toggle for air-gapped
feat(terraform/modules): add state backend helpers and migration scripts
docs(terraform): add READMEs and migration guide
chore(ci): add tfvalidate steps and example apply job
fix(terraform/iam): tighten kms policy for control plane
review_comments: Carlos Mejia: Please ensure GPU node pool exposes a maintenance_window and max_unavailable settings for controlled rolling updates. Also check node label naming to avoid k8s key collisions.
Maya Chen (author): Added maintenance_window and max_unavailable inputs, kept label namespace under 'redwood.' to avoid collisions. Updated README with rollback example.
Priya Singh: IAM policies look good but we should remove s3:* from control plane role; narrow to s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject where possible.
Maya Chen (author): Tightened S3 permissions and added explicit condition for tag:key == 'redwood:deployment'.
Evan Liu: CI plan step failed once due to workspace name collision in the sandbox; added workspace prefixing in example and improved error handling in migrate.sh.
Security Bot: Automated scan flagged an S3 public ACL possibility in the example; updated backend to enforce private ACLs and added notes in migration guide.
release_notes: Added Terraform modules to support Private deployments: GPU node pools, IAM templates, networking primitives and recommended remote state layout. Includes migration guide and example composition.
notes_for_ops: When applying in production, follow terraform/state/migrate.sh with a dry-run plan first and verify remote state locking is functioning (DynamoDB/GCS locks). Avoid enabling preemptible instances in critical workloads. Ensure KMS keys are provisioned in the same region as state buckets.
author_acknowledgement: I confirm I tested the modules in a sandbox environment and updated the docs and migration guide.
